habit_scope: contractor punch then finals then CO. No skip-inspection. CMHC Fig 2 Canadian / confirm AHJ. Goetsch punch process. 2-story light wood only.
how_it_is_done: Do not start punch by skipping a hold that was never called. CMHC p 12, quote: “Municipalities may not inspect the work at every stage of construction; however, most will inspect when the foundations, framing, plumbing and electrical, insulation and exterior finishes are complete.” Schedule them. Know what work must be done and how much notice is required. Confirm with AHJ.

CMHC Ch 2 also names in-stage calls: footings and foundation and municipal services; completed framing including windows, doors, and skylights; completed plumbing, electrical, and mechanical; completed insulation, vapour barrier, and air barrier. Those were P05–P13. If one was missed, it is not a P18 shortcut. Call it. Do not skip inspection.

Contractor assessment. Goetsch Ch 1 closeout applies “regardless of … type from residential to commercial,” quote: the firm “cooperates with the owner, architect, and engineers in developing the punch list, completes all tasks on the punch list, and turns the project over to the owner.”

Goetsch Ch 7 process (skip his college-arena example list — commercial). (1) GC, subs, and trades complete their work. (2) Contractor walks and writes a punch list. (3) Finish that list. (4) Notify the architect the work is complete. (5) Architect walks and writes an architect punch list. (6) Finish that list. (7) Architect rechecks. (8) Architect issues a certificate of substantial completion. (9) GC transfers keys and remaining contractual obligations. (10) Owner issues final payment. Closeout meetings cover O&M manuals, warranties, cleanup, demobilization, subcontractor payments.

Architect punch / substantial completion assumes an architect of record. Gap for production spec SFR with no architect on site. Do not invent a substitute stamp. The AHJ CO is the occupancy paper CMHC names.

CMHC Fig 2 post-construction (Canadian, confirm with AHJ): Completion Inspection (Interior and Exterior) → Certificate of Occupancy. Also: Pre-Occupancy Inspection and Final Plumbing, Heating and Electrical Inspection. Warranty-program extra inspections may apply (CMHC p 12). Confirm with AHJ.

CMHC Ch 2 p 22, quote: “Ensure that all installations have been inspected and function properly and that operating instructions and warranties are provided. A final clean-up of the dwelling concludes the work.” Landscaping may wait for warm weather if the house finishes in fall or winter (CMHC) — that is P17, not a skipped CO.

Goetsch: substantial completion is the architect’s acknowledgement that the owner can occupy even if minor punch items remain; remaining items stay on the certificate. Liquidated damages talk in Goetsch is contract language, not an AHJ skip. Do not treat substantial completion as a reason to skip the CO inspection.
